boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of North Carolina Wilmington
boards.description: Ten currently listed late-hour food, dessert, pizza, and convenience destinations in Wilmington, with official location pages checked on August 13, 2026.

cards.title: Buffaloe's
cards.subtitle: 4924 Wrightsville Avenue, Wilmington
cards.notes: Use the official hour list before heading out; grill service runs later Thursday through Saturday than the other days.
cards.short_summary: A Wrightsville Avenue grill, deli, snacks, and ice-cream stop with overnight hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Buffaloe's lists grill hours through 12:30 AM Sunday–Wednesday and 2:30 AM Thursday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Buffaloe's — Grill · Snacks · Deli · Ice Cream · Wilmington, NC
cards.access_notes: Official site lists the shop open until 1 AM Sunday–Wednesday and 3 AM Thursday–Saturday; grill closes 30 minutes earlier.

cards.title: Taco Bell on South College
cards.subtitle: 630 S College Rd, Wilmington
cards.notes: Check whether you want dining room or drive-thru access; the official location page posts hours for each separately.
cards.short_summary: A South College Road restaurant with posted late drive-thru and dine-in service.
cards.evidence_claim: The location lists drive-thru service until 4 AM most nights and 5 AM Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell® in Wilmington, NC — 630 S College Rd
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru until 4 AM Sunday–Thursday and 5 AM Friday–Saturday; dine-in hours are separately posted.

cards.title: Taco Bell on North College
cards.subtitle: 2600 N College Rd, Wilmington
cards.notes: Use the North College Road location when its posted late drive-thru hours fit your route; verify the day before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A separate Taco Bell location on North College Road with late-night service.
cards.evidence_claim: The location lists drive-thru service until 3 AM most nights and 4 AM Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell® in Wilmington, NC — 2600 N College Rd
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru and dine-in service until 3 AM Sunday–Thursday and 4 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Wendy's University Center
cards.subtitle: 350 South College Road, Wilmington
cards.notes: Confirm restaurant versus drive-thru service on the official locator, then plan around the later Friday and Saturday closing time.
cards.short_summary: A University Center Wendy's with restaurant and drive-thru hours into early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy's lists restaurant and drive-thru hours until 2 AM Sunday–Thursday and 3 AM Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Wendy's University Center — 350 South College Road
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists restaurant and drive-thru service until 2 AM Sunday–Thursday and 3 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Papa Johns on Oleander
cards.subtitle: 5814 Oleander Dr, Ste 1, Wilmington
cards.notes: Order ahead if using the late window, and distinguish delivery from carryout because the listed closing times differ.
cards.short_summary: An Oleander Drive pizza location with delivery and carryout into early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Papa Johns lists delivery until 2 AM most nights and 3 AM Thursday–Saturday; carryout runs 20 minutes earlier.
cards.source_title: Papa Johns Oleander Dr — Wilmington, NC
cards.access_notes: Official page lists delivery until 2 AM Sunday–Wednesday and 3 AM Thursday–Saturday; carryout ends at 1:40 AM or 2:40 AM.

cards.title: Domino's on College Acres
cards.subtitle: 4714 College Acres Dr, Wilmington
cards.notes: Use the official Domino's locator to check today’s close before ordering, since the location page identifies it as open until 1 AM.
cards.short_summary: A College Acres Drive pizza location with a listed 1 AM closing time.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino's official Wilmington location listing identifies the 4714 College Acres Drive store as open until 1 AM.
cards.access_notes: The official Domino's Wilmington page lists the nearby 4714 College Acres Dr location as open until 1 AM.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies
cards.subtitle: 1040 S College Rd, Wilmington
cards.notes: Use the official store page to start a pickup or delivery order, especially when its late-night schedule is the deciding factor.
cards.short_summary: A S College Road cookie shop whose official store page advertises delivery until 3 AM daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies' official Wilmington store page states that warm cookies are delivered until 3 AM daily.
cards.access_notes: Official store page advertises warm-cookie delivery until 3 AM daily; confirm pickup availability in the ordering flow.

cards.title: Taqueria La Tapatia
cards.subtitle: 820 College Rd, Wilmington
cards.notes: Plan around the day-specific schedule: Friday is the latest posted closing, while Sunday remains open later than weekdays.
cards.short_summary: A College Road taqueria across from campus with late Friday and Sunday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Taqueria La Tapatia lists hours until 11 PM Friday and until 10 PM Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists closing at 9:30 PM Monday–Thursday and Saturday, 11 PM Friday, and 10 PM Sunday.

cards.title: Yoshi Sushi on Racine
cards.subtitle: 260 Racine Dr, Wilmington
cards.notes: For a later evening order, use the official online ordering page and note that Friday and Saturday have the latest posted hours.
cards.short_summary: A Racine Drive sushi and noodle restaurant near UNCW with a 10 PM weekend close.
cards.evidence_claim: Yoshi Sushi lists business hours until 10 PM Friday and Saturday, with carryout until 9:30 PM.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists business hours until 10 PM Friday–Saturday and carryout until 9:30 PM; other days close earlier.

cards.title: Mobil on North College
cards.subtitle: 425 N College Road, Wilmington
cards.notes: Use the official station locator for a late convenience-store stop, and check its listed services before making a special trip.
cards.short_summary: A North College Road Mobil station with a convenience store and nightly 2 AM closing.
cards.evidence_claim: Mobil lists the station at 425 N College Road open from 5 AM until 2 AM every day and identifies a convenience store service.
cards.source_title: Mobil at 425 N. College Road — Wilmington, NC
cards.access_notes: Official ExxonMobil locator lists location hours of 5 AM–2 AM Monday through Sunday and a convenience store.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Named UNCW campus spaces for studying, meeting, programs, and recreation; check current building or facility rules before visiting.

cards.title: Randall Library Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Randall Library, first floor
cards.notes: Use the first-floor Learning Commons for computer-based work, printing, or a study reset; iPrint locations identify both its common area and guest-computer area.
cards.short_summary: A practical first-floor study and technology stop in Randall Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists iPrint stations in Randall Library’s first-floor Learning Commons Area and Guest Computer Area.
cards.access_notes: Library services and access may vary by term; confirm current library hours before going.

cards.title: Fisher Student Center
cards.subtitle: Campus Life facility
cards.notes: Meet collaborators in the building’s common areas, then use its event-space directory to identify a room for a planned gathering or presentation.
cards.short_summary: A Campus Life building with gathering spaces and the Lumina Theater.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW identifies the Fisher Student Center as a Campus Life facility with smaller meeting and gathering spaces.
cards.access_notes: Campus Life building hours and individual room availability vary; some uses require a reservation.

cards.title: Clock Tower Lounge
cards.subtitle: Fisher Student Center, room FSC 2000
cards.notes: Bring a small group or reading task to the permanent seating and tables, and take in the Campus Commons view from the wraparound windows.
cards.short_summary: A furnished lounge with Campus Commons views and a veranda.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW describes Clock Tower Lounge as having comfortable seating, small tables, a fireplace, large windows, and veranda access.
cards.access_notes: This is an event space; confirm whether it is open or reserved before relying on it for study.

cards.title: Lumina Theater
cards.subtitle: Fisher Student Center
cards.notes: Check the Campus Life calendar for film programming, panels, or presentations; the theater is a defined multi-use auditorium rather than a general lounge.
cards.short_summary: A campus auditorium used for films, panels, and presentations.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW says Lumina Theater in the Fisher Student Center is a multi-use auditorium for film programming, presentations, panels, and more.
cards.access_notes: Attend scheduled programming or arrange use through Campus Life; access is not guaranteed outside events.

cards.title: Fisher University Union
cards.subtitle: Campus Life facility
cards.notes: Use the Union as a coordination point for campus services, cultural hubs, or a reserved gathering; check the building directory for the office or room you need.
cards.short_summary: A Campus Life hub with services, cultural spaces, and event rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW states that Fisher University Union provides passport and mailing services and houses cultural hubs for African American and Latinx community members.
cards.access_notes: Campus Life building hours vary; offices and reservable rooms have their own availability.

cards.title: Town Square
cards.subtitle: Fisher University Union common area
cards.notes: Walk through when looking for fair tables or small exhibitions, and use the space as an easy landmark for meeting someone in the Union.
cards.short_summary: A Union common area designed for tabling and small exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW describes Town Square as a Fisher University Union common area with foot traffic, suitable for fair tabling and small exhibitions.
cards.access_notes: Tabling and exhibitions are managed uses; check Campus Life procedures before setting up.

cards.title: Warwick Center
cards.subtitle: Campus Life facility
cards.notes: Stop here to find campus dining, departments, and services, or choose a quiet spot to pause between classes; check the building directory for current occupants.
cards.short_summary: A Campus Life building that combines services, dining, and informal space.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW says the Warwick Center hosts university departments, campus dining locations, and community services, and its facilities include lounges for friends or group work.
cards.access_notes: Campus Life facility hours vary by term; confirm the current schedule before visiting.

cards.title: University Commons
cards.subtitle: Campus Life outdoor focal point
cards.notes: Use this named outdoor Campus Life area as a meetup point before an event, and check university event listings for any scheduled programming that changes access.
cards.short_summary: A named Campus Life outdoor area associated with campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW’s Code of Student Life identifies University Commons as one of the facilities serving as focal points for campus life outside the classroom.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access can be affected by scheduled events, weather, and university operations.

cards.title: UNCW Amphitheater
cards.subtitle: Campus Life outdoor performance venue
cards.notes: Check for scheduled performances or student-organization programming, then use the amphitheater as a recognizable outdoor meeting point on the Campus Life side of campus.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor Campus Life venue for campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW’s Code of Student Life lists the Amphitheater among facilities that provide performance venues and serve as focal points for campus life.
cards.access_notes: Event activity and campus operations may affect access; follow posted university guidance.

cards.title: Shoreline Sports Complex
cards.subtitle: Between Pat Leonard Student Recreation Center and Terrapin/Pelican Hall
cards.notes: Plan an outdoor activity around the courts, fields, or fitness area, and check the posted facility schedule before arriving because programming can take priority.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor recreation complex with courts, fields, fitness equipment, and a pavilion.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists sand-volleyball, basketball, and tennis/pickleball courts, grass fields, an outdoor fitness area, and a pavilion at Shoreline Sports Complex.
cards.access_notes: Current UNCW students, faculty/staff, and their guests may use it; scheduled activities take priority. Facility page lists lights until 11 p.m. during the academic year.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission hangs at UNCW and nearby Wilmington public spaces.

cards.title: Browse the CAB Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Cultural Arts Building, UNCW
cards.notes: Walk through the ground-floor exhibition space, then use the posted gallery hours to plan a low-key art stop between classes.
cards.short_summary: Free public exhibitions in UNCW’s Cultural Arts Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Entrance to CAB Art Gallery exhibitions is free of charge and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Gallery hours listed by UNCW are Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; summer hours differ. Check the page before going.

cards.title: See work in the Mezzanine Gallery
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Cultural Arts Building, UNCW
cards.notes: Take the stairs or elevator to the second-floor gallery and spend time with the changing student solo, group, and curated exhibits.
cards.short_summary: A separate UNCW gallery for changing student-focused exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: All Mezzanine Gallery exhibitions and lectures are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of the Cultural Arts Building; confirm current exhibition timing before visiting.

cards.title: Check out the Sherman Hayes Gallery
cards.subtitle: First floor, UNCW Library
cards.notes: Visit the first-floor library gallery to view its rotating art or materials displays; pair it with library time or a campus walk.
cards.short_summary: A library-based UNCW gallery with public events and exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: Sherman Hayes Gallery events are free and open to the public, and the gallery is open whenever UNCW Library is open.
cards.access_notes: On the first floor near TAC; follow current UNCW Library opening hours.

cards.title: Hike Ev-Henwood Nature Preserve
cards.subtitle: UNCW-managed preserve near Town Creek
cards.notes: Choose a daylight walk on the preserve trails and pause at the old reservoir or logging-channel remnants described on UNCW’s trail information.
cards.short_summary: A public UNCW nature preserve for hiking, photography, and birdwatching.
cards.evidence_claim: Ev-Henwood is open to the public with no charge for admission and is open dawn to dusk, seven days a week.
cards.access_notes: Open dawn to dusk daily. Groups and night access have additional guidance on the UNCW page.

cards.title: Walk the Japanese Garden
cards.subtitle: New Hanover County Arboretum, 6206 Oleander Drive
cards.notes: Enter beneath the torii gateways and follow the garden’s paths past the tea house and stream at a calm, unhurried pace.
cards.short_summary: A named Arboretum garden with a tea house, dry gardens, and stream.
cards.evidence_claim: The New Hanover County Arboretum is free and open to the public daily; its Japanese Garden has a tea house, dry gardens, and a dragon-like stream.
cards.source_title: Demonstration Gardens | New Hanover County, NC
cards.access_notes: The Arboretum says it is free and open daily 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; occasional private-event closures are possible.

cards.title: Stroll the Camellia Walk
cards.subtitle: New Hanover County Arboretum, 6206 Oleander Drive
cards.notes: Follow the walk’s camellia collection and look for the Royal Velvet Camellia sculpture; return in the cooler months for seasonal blooms.
cards.short_summary: A named Arboretum walk with more than 130 camellia shrubs.
cards.evidence_claim: The New Hanover County Arboretum is free and open to the public daily, and Camellia Walk includes over 130 camellia shrubs.
cards.source_title: Demonstration Gardens | New Hanover County, NC
cards.access_notes: The Arboretum is free to visit and normally requires no ticket; daily garden hours are 8 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.title: Read the Native Plant Garden displays
cards.subtitle: New Hanover County Arboretum, 6206 Oleander Drive
cards.notes: Use the educational signs and murals to identify Cape Fear-region plants, then compare the displays with what you notice around campus.
cards.short_summary: A named garden featuring local plants and educational interpretation.
cards.evidence_claim: The New Hanover County Arboretum is free and open to the public daily; its Native Plant Garden showcases Cape Fear-region plants and educational murals.
cards.source_title: Demonstration Gardens | New Hanover County, NC
cards.access_notes: The Arboretum is free to visit and normally requires no ticket; avoid dates when it is closed for a private event.

cards.title: Follow the Contemplation Garden labyrinth
cards.subtitle: New Hanover County Arboretum, 6206 Oleander Drive
cards.notes: Walk the labyrinth path beneath the five flags, keeping the visit quiet and respectful of the garden’s military-honoring purpose.
cards.short_summary: A named reflection garden with a labyrinth walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The New Hanover County Arboretum is free and open to the public daily; the Contemplation Garden includes a labyrinth walk beneath five flags.
cards.source_title: Demonstration Gardens | New Hanover County, NC
cards.access_notes: The Arboretum is free to visit and normally requires no ticket; daily garden hours are 8 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.title: Bring a no-cost picnic to the Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Between Camellia Walk and Japanese Garden, New Hanover County Arboretum
cards.notes: Bring food from home and use the shaded picnic tables between Camellia Walk and the Japanese Garden on a first-come basis.
cards.short_summary: A first-come picnic spot inside the free county Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arboretum is free and open to the public daily, and its shaded picnic area has first-come, first-served tables between Camellia Walk and the Japanese Garden.
cards.source_title: Visitor Etiquette | New Hanover County, NC
cards.access_notes: Tables are first-come, first-served. The Arboretum is generally open daily 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; call ahead for possible private-event closure.

cards.title: Spend time in Riverfront Park’s East Garden
cards.subtitle: Riverfront Park, downtown Wilmington
cards.notes: Use the Nutt Street Promenade entrance to reach the East Garden, then take in the riverfront setting without entering ticketed amphitheater events.
cards.short_summary: A publicly accessible garden area at Wilmington’s riverfront park.
cards.evidence_claim: Riverfront Park is open to the public from sunrise to sunset, and its East Garden is open daily, including on concert dates.
cards.access_notes: Open sunrise to sunset except during city-approved events or programs; on concert dates, access the East Garden through Nutt Street Promenade.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented study environments across UNCW Library’s Discovery Hall and Randall Hall, with access details noted where the library specifies them.

cards.title: Grand Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Discovery Hall, third floor
cards.notes: Use the semi-private carrels for individual work, and keep conversations elsewhere: the room is designated for quiet study only.
cards.short_summary: A silent-study room with ample seating and 12 semi-private carrels.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW identifies DH3001 as a non-reservable, quiet-study-only Grand Reading Room with a 105-person maximum capacity; its expansion page notes 12 semi-private study carrels.
cards.source_title: Space Usage and Reservation Guidelines | UNCW Library
cards.access_notes: Not reservable. Quiet study only; covered drinks are allowed but food is not.

cards.title: The Lookout
cards.subtitle: Discovery Hall, third floor
cards.notes: Settle in by the campus-facing windows for reading or planning; bring only a covered drink, since food is not allowed.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor library space with expansive campus views and a mural.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW describes The Lookout as a third-floor space with expansive windows overlooking campus, and library guidelines list it as DH3013, non-reservable, with a capacity of 30.
cards.access_notes: Not reservable; maximum capacity 30. Covered drinks only and no food.

cards.title: The Living Room
cards.subtitle: Randall Hall, UNCW Library
cards.notes: Bring a collaborative task and use the shared seating; this is an open space, so keep adjacent quiet-study areas in mind.
cards.short_summary: A shared Randall Hall setting designated for collaboration and study.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW’s library expansion page identifies The Living Room as a gathering space for collaboration and study; library guidelines state it is first-come, first-served.
cards.access_notes: Open, first-come, first-served shared space. Food and drink are permitted; expected group-activity noise should remain respectful.

cards.title: Sensory Friendly Study Space
cards.subtitle: Randall Hall 2017
cards.notes: Adjust the desk, lamp, or seating to suit your focus needs, then return the setup when leaving and use headphones for audio.
cards.short_summary: A customizable individual-study room with sensory-support tools.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists RL2017 as a non-reservable sensory-friendly space for eligible OneCard holders, with adjustable desks, dimmable lamps, seating options, and noise-reduction headsets.
cards.source_title: Sensory Friendly Study Space | UNCW Library
cards.access_notes: Available to UNCW students, faculty, and staff with a valid OneCard; intended for individual study. Not reservable.

cards.title: Graduate Student Study Space
cards.subtitle: Randall Hall 2048
cards.notes: Graduate students can use this card-access space for focused work; check the reservation system separately if a graduate study room is needed.
cards.short_summary: A graduate-only study area with seating, technology, and adjoining study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW identifies RL2048 as an expanded Graduate Student Study Space and states that it is non-reservable, accessible to graduate students by OneCard tap, and has a capacity of 45.
cards.source_title: Space Usage and Reservation Guidelines | UNCW Library
cards.access_notes: Accessible only to graduate students through OneCard tap. The main space is not reservable.

cards.title: Retreat at Randall
cards.subtitle: Randall Hall 2016
cards.notes: Use this named Randall Hall retreat for individual study, and follow the room’s food restriction so the environment remains suitable for everyone.
cards.short_summary: A card-access study space included in UNCW Library’s documented space inventory.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW Library’s space guidelines list Retreat at Randall (RL2016) among its named spaces, and the library privacy policy identifies it as a space requiring OneCard access.
cards.source_title: Space Usage and Reservation Guidelines | UNCW Library
cards.access_notes: OneCard access is required. Library general guidance specifically identifies Retreat at Randall as a space where food is not allowed.

cards.entity_name: Center for Southeast North Carolina Archives and History Research Room
cards.title: Archives Research Room
cards.subtitle: Discovery Hall, second floor
cards.notes: Plan an archive-based research session around the room’s adjacent books, manuscript collections, maps, photographs, and audiovisual materials.
cards.short_summary: A research room beside UNCW archival and special-collections materials.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW states that Discovery Hall’s second floor includes the Center for Southeast North Carolina Archives and History and a unified research room adjacent to its books and manuscript collections.
cards.access_notes: Consult the library before a visit for current research-room procedures and collection access.

cards.title: Visualization and Analysis Lab
cards.subtitle: Discovery Hall 1072
cards.notes: Use this lab when a project needs large-scale visual work; contact library facilities first about collaboration, class, event, or presentation use.
cards.short_summary: A data-visualization lab centered on a 30-foot display wall.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW describes DH1072 as a Visualization and Analysis Lab with an immersive 30-foot video display wall, a high-performance computer, and use for visualization-related classes, events, presentations, and collaboration.
cards.access_notes: For classes, events, presentations, or visualization collaboration; UNCW directs users to contact rlfacility@uncw.edu for details.

cards.title: Study Room RL1001C4
cards.subtitle: Randall Hall, first floor
cards.notes: Reserve this six-seat room for a small group or use it when unreserved; take advantage of the whiteboard, power, and movable tables.
cards.short_summary: A six-seat, accessible study room with natural light and a whiteboard.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists RL1001C4 as a first-floor Randall Hall study room for six with natural light, movable tables and chairs, power, and a wall-mounted whiteboard.
cards.access_notes: Current UNCW students, staff, and faculty may reserve it. When unreserved, it is first-come, first-served.

cards.entity_name: Discovery Hall Third-Floor Open Study Areas
cards.title: Discovery Hall Third-Floor Open Study Areas
cards.subtitle: Discovery Hall, third floor
cards.notes: Choose an open seat for independent work and keep your volume low: Discovery Hall’s third floor is designated as a quiet space.
cards.short_summary: Open third-floor study seating with nearby computing and printing.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW identifies Discovery Hall’s third floor as containing open study areas, open computing, and iPrint stations; its noise policy designates the floor as a quiet space.
cards.access_notes: Open study area, not a reservable room. Keep noise to a minimum and keep phones on silent, per the library noise policy.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on College Road, Racine Drive, Kerr Avenue, Randall Parkway, and Emerson Street that UNCW currently serves with off-campus shuttles.

cards.title: College Road at Harris Teeter
cards.subtitle: College Road corridor • 710 Red Shuttle stop 1156
cards.notes: Use this College Road stop when the 710 Red Shuttle is running; confirm the current route map and service calendar before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A named College Road destination on UNCW’s Red Shuttle route.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists “College Rd at Harris Teeter (1156)” as a stop on the 710 Red Shuttle.
cards.access_notes: UNCW publishes this as an off-campus shuttle stop; check the current shuttle schedule before travel.

cards.title: University Commons
cards.subtitle: New Centre Drive corridor • 710 Red and 712 Teal stop 1312
cards.notes: Plan this stop as a transfer-friendly off-campus destination: both the 710 Red and 712 Teal routes list it in their current stop sequences.
cards.short_summary: A named University Commons stop served by two UNCW shuttle routes.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists “New Center at University Commons (1312)” on both the 710 Red and 712 Teal shuttles.
cards.access_notes: UNCW identifies University Commons as a stop on both routes; consult the active schedule and route map.

cards.title: Racine Drive at Wilmington Commons
cards.subtitle: Racine Drive corridor • 710 Red and 712 Teal stop 1911
cards.notes: Use the northbound Racine Drive stop for Wilmington Commons; check which shuttle is in service, since UNCW lists it on two routes.
cards.short_summary: A northbound Racine Drive stop for Wilmington Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists “Racine Dr at Wilmington Commons NB (1911)” on the 710 Red and 712 Teal shuttles.
cards.access_notes: UNCW’s route page identifies this northbound stop; service timing varies by route and academic calendar.

cards.title: Kerr Avenue and Hoggard Drive
cards.subtitle: Kerr Avenue corridor • 710 Red Shuttle stop 1414
cards.notes: Use this named Kerr Avenue intersection as a Red Shuttle waypoint, and review the live service information before relying on the stop.
cards.short_summary: A Kerr Avenue intersection listed on UNCW’s Red Shuttle route.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists “Kerr Ave & Hoggard Dr (1414)” as a 710 Red Shuttle stop.
cards.access_notes: This is a current UNCW off-campus shuttle stop; verify operating days and route updates before travel.

cards.title: Kerr Avenue at Candlewyck
cards.subtitle: Kerr Avenue corridor • 710 Red Shuttle stop 1415
cards.notes: Follow the Red Shuttle’s listed sequence along Kerr Avenue and use this northbound Candlewyck stop as the marked destination.
cards.short_summary: A named northbound stop on the Kerr Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists “Kerr Ave at Candlewyck NB (1415)” as a 710 Red Shuttle stop.
cards.access_notes: UNCW lists this northbound stop on the Red route; review the current route map before departure.

cards.title: Kerr Avenue at Patrick
cards.subtitle: Kerr Avenue corridor • 710 Red Shuttle stop 1417
cards.notes: Use the listed northbound Kerr Avenue at Patrick stop when navigating the Red Shuttle corridor, after checking the day’s service status.
cards.short_summary: A second named Kerr Avenue waypoint on the Red Shuttle.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists “Kerr Ave at Patrick NB (1417)” as a 710 Red Shuttle stop.
cards.access_notes: UNCW identifies this northbound stop on the Red route; confirm current operations before using it.

cards.title: Randall Parkway at Campus Cove
cards.subtitle: Randall Parkway corridor • 710 Red and 711 Grey stop 1481
cards.notes: Choose this Randall Parkway stop for a route overlap: UNCW lists Campus Cove on both the Red and Grey off-campus shuttles.
cards.short_summary: A Campus Cove stop shared by UNCW’s Red and Grey routes.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists “Randall Pkwy at Campus Cove (1481)” on the 710 Red and 711 Grey shuttles.
cards.access_notes: UNCW’s route page identifies this stop on two routes; check the current timetable for each service.

cards.title: Emerson Street at Aspire 349
cards.subtitle: Emerson Street corridor • 710 Red and 711 Grey stop 1466
cards.notes: Use this Emerson Street destination when either Red or Grey service is active; UNCW includes the same named stop on both routes.
cards.short_summary: An Emerson Street shuttle destination shared by two routes.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists “Emerson St at Aspire 349 (1466)” on the 710 Red and 711 Grey shuttles.
cards.access_notes: UNCW lists this destination on Red and Grey shuttle sequences; verify current service before travel.

cards.title: Randall Parkway at Plato's Lofts
cards.subtitle: Randall Parkway corridor • 711 Grey Shuttle stop 1472
cards.notes: Start or end a Grey Shuttle trip at this named Randall Parkway stop; UNCW’s published route sequence identifies it as the first trip’s start point.
cards.short_summary: The listed starting point for UNCW’s Grey Shuttle service.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW states that the 711 Grey Shuttle’s first trip starts at “Plato’s Lofts” and lists “Randall Pkwy at Plato’s Lofts (1472)” as a stop.
cards.access_notes: UNCW publishes this as a Grey Shuttle stop and start point; confirm the current weekday service schedule.

cards.title: Randall Parkway at The Nest
cards.subtitle: Randall Parkway corridor • 711 Grey Shuttle stop 1456
cards.notes: Use this Randall Parkway stop as a distinct Grey Shuttle destination; consult the current UNCW shuttle schedule for operating dates and timing.
cards.short_summary: A named Randall Parkway destination on UNCW’s Grey route.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists “Randall Pkwy at The Nest (1456)” as a stop on the 711 Grey Shuttle.
cards.access_notes: UNCW’s route page lists this on the Grey Shuttle; review current operating times before travel.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented UNCW rituals and recurring campus events, from teal-wearing Tuesdays to the first-year class photo.

cards.title: Wear Teal on Tuesday
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide UNCW spirit tradition
cards.notes: Plan one teal item for Tuesday and join students, faculty and staff in displaying UNCW’s officially recognized primary color.
cards.short_summary: A weekly campus ritual centered on UNCW teal.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW identifies Teal Tuesday as a campus tradition in which students, faculty and staff display the school color.
cards.access_notes: Wear teal anywhere on campus on Tuesdays.

cards.title: Spot the Mace at Convocation
cards.subtitle: Formal academic ceremonies
cards.notes: At convocation or commencement, watch for the mace carried by the chief faculty marshal and notice its regional and university materials.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial mace leads UNCW’s major academic observances.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW states that its mace is carried by the chief faculty marshal at commencement and convocation.
cards.access_notes: Observe during scheduled convocation or commencement ceremonies.

cards.title: Unveil the Class Flag
cards.subtitle: New-student convocation
cards.notes: New students can take part in the convocation flag unveiling, then use the class marker as a simple record of their entering cohort.
cards.short_summary: Each incoming class begins the year by unveiling its flag.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW says incoming freshmen unveil their class flag as part of the start-of-year tradition.
cards.access_notes: Participation is part of new-student convocation programming.

cards.title: Join the Giant Class Photo
cards.subtitle: New-student convocation
cards.notes: Arrive with your incoming class for the traditional class photo, a shared first-year moment held before the formal convocation program.
cards.short_summary: Incoming Seahawks gather for a cohort portrait at the academic year’s opening.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW documents a traditional class photo for incoming freshmen at the beginning of each academic year.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled with new-student convocation activities.

cards.title: Make the Trek to Trask
cards.subtitle: Trask Coliseum • new academic year
cards.notes: Follow the incoming class to Trask Coliseum for formal convocation and hear UNCW’s academic expectations from university leadership and faculty.
cards.short_summary: A collective walk to Trask marks the official opening of the year.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW says incoming freshmen make the trek to Trask Coliseum for the formal convocation ceremony.
cards.access_notes: For new students during the annual convocation program.

cards.title: Gather for Homecoming TEALgate
cards.subtitle: UNCW Homecoming
cards.notes: Check the Homecoming schedule, wear teal and take part in the family-oriented TEALgate gathering connected to the men’s basketball game.
cards.short_summary: Teal attire and basketball anchor UNCW’s Homecoming gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists Homecoming TEALgate and a men’s basketball game among its Homecoming traditions.
cards.access_notes: Occurs as part of the annual Homecoming schedule; confirm current event details.

cards.title: See Homecoming Royalty Announced
cards.subtitle: Men’s basketball halftime • Homecoming
cards.notes: Attend the Homecoming basketball game and watch halftime for the announcement of Homecoming royalty and recognition of alumni award winners.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming royalty is revealed at halftime of the men’s basketball game.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW states that Homecoming royalty is announced at halftime of the men’s basketball game.
cards.access_notes: Timing depends on the annual Homecoming basketball game.

cards.title: Start Homecoming Week at Late Night Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Wagoner Dining Hall • spring Homecoming Week
cards.notes: During spring Homecoming Week, head to Wagoner for the faculty-and-staff-served breakfast, Sammy photos and the annual Lip Sync Battle.
cards.short_summary: A breakfast gathering launches UNCW’s spring Homecoming Week.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW describes Late Night Breakfast as the kick-off to spring Homecoming Week, with breakfast served by faculty and staff.
cards.access_notes: UNCW labels the event “Late Night Breakfast”; verify the current Homecoming schedule and dining access before going.

cards.title: Share the Wagsgiving Meal
cards.subtitle: Wagoner Dining Hall • before Thanksgiving break
cards.notes: Before Thanksgiving break, look for UNCW’s Thanksgiving-themed Wagsgiving meal at Wagoner Dining Hall and confirm the dining schedule for the date.
cards.short_summary: A Thanksgiving-themed Wagoner meal sends students toward break.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW identifies Wagsgiving as a Thanksgiving-themed meal at Wagoner Dining Hall before Thanksgiving break.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the annual date and applicable dining access with UNCW Dining.

cards.title: Fall into the Dub
cards.subtitle: First semester • campus-wide welcome events
cards.notes: Use the first-semester Fall into the Dub calendar to sample welcome activities, meet student leaders and learn how to stay involved on campus.
cards.short_summary: A first-semester welcome series helps students connect with UNCW.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW describes Fall into the Dub as a move-in-to-first-semester series of events and activities welcoming students to the UNCW community.
cards.access_notes: Events occur throughout the first semester; consult the current campus calendar.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of North Carolina Wilmington, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A flexible, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence that begins on campus and branches into documented Wilmington activities.

cards.title: Get Oriented with the Campus Map
cards.subtitle: Start at UNCW’s main campus
cards.notes: Open the interactive map before heading out, then use it to locate buildings, parking, and the next stops in your own walking route.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for turning a new campus into a navigable place.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW provides an interactive main-campus map with building, parking, and location details.
cards.access_notes: Use the interactive map for current destination and parking details.

cards.title: Find Randall Library
cards.subtitle: UNCW campus
cards.notes: Take a pass through Randall Library and save its floor maps for later; they identify spaces in both Randall Hall and Discovery Hall.
cards.short_summary: A campus landmark with official floor maps to keep handy after the weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW Library publishes floor maps for Randall Hall and Discovery Hall.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours and access information before visiting.

cards.title: See What’s Showing at Boseman Gallery
cards.subtitle: Fisher University Union
cards.notes: Stop by the gallery in the Fisher University Union, then check the exhibition page to see which student, local, or regional work is on view.
cards.short_summary: A year-round campus gallery with changing exhibitions and a permanent collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ann Flack Boseman Gallery displays varied media year-round and schedules five exhibitions annually featuring UNCW, local, and regional artists.
cards.access_notes: Review the current exhibition listing before making a dedicated trip.

cards.title: Check the Lumina Theater Calendar
cards.subtitle: First floor, Fisher Student Center
cards.notes: Look for a film, lecture, panel, or concert that fits your weekend. Confirm the specific program’s ticketing and entry details before you go.
cards.short_summary: A 333-seat campus theater set up for films and other public-facing programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Lumina Theater is on the first floor of the Fisher Student Center and supports film programming, lectures, panels, and concerts.
cards.access_notes: Programming and admission vary by event; consult the event listing before attending.

cards.title: Watch for a UNCWeekends BINGO Night
cards.subtitle: Recurring UNCW weekend programming
cards.notes: Check WaveLink for an upcoming themed BINGO Night and bring a friend; UNCWeekends lists it among its recurring campus activities.
cards.short_summary: A documented alcohol-free weekend activity hosted through UNCW Campus Activities.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCWeekends lists themed BINGO Night among the activities it hosts and provides alcohol-free options every weekend during the academic year.
cards.access_notes: Available during the academic year; use WaveLink to confirm the date, location, and entry details.

cards.title: Make Time for a Campus Craft
cards.subtitle: Recurring UNCWeekends activity
cards.notes: Look for a Catching Up With the Crafts session on WaveLink and join the posted activity; UNCWeekends supplies the materials for this program.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on, alcohol-free option that can anchor a low-key campus afternoon.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCWeekends identifies Catching Up With the Crafts as an activity where the program brings the supplies.
cards.access_notes: Dates and locations vary; confirm the posted event details on WaveLink.

cards.title: Check Out the Rec Center
cards.subtitle: UNCW campus recreation
cards.notes: Ask about student access and available activities at the recreation center, then choose an option that fits your group and the facility schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation destination connected to UNCW’s health and wellness programming.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW Campus Recreation identifies the Pat Leonard Student Recreation Center as one of its facilities and programs supporting student wellbeing.
cards.access_notes: Facility access and activity availability depend on membership status and the current schedule.

cards.title: See Whether the Seahawks Are Home
cards.subtitle: UNCW campus athletics venue
cards.notes: Check the current athletics schedule for a home game, then plan around the posted start time and ticket information for Trask Coliseum.
cards.short_summary: UNCW’s basketball home floor and a recurring setting for campus game days.
cards.evidence_claim: Trask Coliseum is the home floor for UNCW’s men’s and women’s basketball teams.
cards.source_title: Trask Coliseum - Facilities | UNC Wilmington Athletics
cards.access_notes: Game schedules, ticket requirements, and door times vary by event; verify them with UNCW Athletics.

cards.title: Add an Art-Museum Detour
cards.subtitle: 3201 South 17th Street, Wilmington
cards.notes: Plan a daytime museum visit around the rotating exhibitions and outdoor spaces. Bring a current local university or college student ID for the stated student admission policy.
cards.short_summary: A Wilmington museum with rotating exhibitions, outdoor grounds, and a documented local-student admission option.
cards.evidence_claim: Cameron Art Museum is open Tuesday through Sunday, with Thursday hours until 9 p.m., and states that local university and community-college students receive free admission.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Cameron Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Current hours are Tuesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; Thursdays are open until 9 p.m. Verify closures and bring qualifying student ID.

cards.title: Finish with a Beach Walk
cards.subtitle: 25 East Salisbury Street, Wrightsville Beach
cards.notes: Use the town-listed access for an oceanfront walk and its restroom, shower, gazebo, and ADA-accessible route; follow posted beach conditions and rules.
cards.short_summary: A named public beach access with amenities documented by the Town of Wrightsville Beach.
cards.evidence_claim: Wrightsville Beach Access Number 16 at 25 East Salisbury Street has parking, an ADA-accessible route, a gazebo, restrooms, and a shower, and is listed as open year-round from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m.
cards.source_title: Beach Accesses, Public Restrooms, & Lifeguard Stand Locations | Wrightsville Beach, NC
cards.access_notes: Town-listed access hours are 7 a.m.–9 p.m., year-round. Parking availability and fees may apply; check the town’s current parking information.
